## Background

Automatic refresh should be invisible when Beadwork and git are healthy. It must not, however, make the user lose the last good Issue List because a refresh probe or a Beadwork command briefly fails. The existing initial-load failure presentation is appropriate when no Issue List exists yet, but it is too disruptive after a successful snapshot is already visible.

ADR-0007 distinguishes transient failures from structural failures. This slice makes that distinction user-visible and consistent across automatic ref-change refreshes, while retaining the last known good Issue List.

## What to build

When automatic refresh encounters a temporary error, keep the visible Issue List unchanged and retry silently. After five consecutive failures of the same transient class, show a non-disruptive banner above the list explaining that automatic refresh is failing.

When the problem is structural — `git` missing from PATH, `bw` missing from PATH, or a Workspace that is not a Beadwork Workspace — show the same banner immediately. Never replace an already-rendered Issue List with the initial full-pane failure state solely because an automatic refresh failed.

## Technical Approach

- Add a refresh-specific error classifier at the backend boundary. It distinguishes ref-probe failures, Beadwork loader failures, missing `git`, missing `bw`, invalid Beadwork Workspace, and no-Current-Workspace idle state.
- Maintain failure counters per transient class. A successful operation for that class resets its counter; structural failures bypass the retry budget.
- Publish typed refresh failure events through the same refresh event contract as successful updates. Include workspace identity, workspace-selection generation, refresh revision, error kind, message, and whether the error is transient.
- Extend frontend refresh state with non-blocking banner presentation. The banner is admitted only for the active Workspace and refresh generation; the last successful `IssueExplorerLoadState` remains rendered below it.
- Preserve the existing full-pane error behavior for a first load that has no last good snapshot.

## Considerations

- The ref probe and the three Beadwork view loaders can fail independently. A successful SHA probe must not erase a pending loader-failure count, and a successful loader must not hide a still-failing probe.
- Missing `git` is new user-facing dependency behavior introduced by ADR-0007; the banner must state why git is needed.
- No Current Workspace is not an error. The refresh service is idle in that state and must not increment a counter or show a banner.
- The banner is for refresh health, not Workspace switching validation; do not merge it with unrelated workspace-selector errors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One through four consecutive transient ref-probe or loader failures leave the last good Issue List visible with no banner.
- [ ] Five consecutive failures of one transient class show a refresh banner while retaining the last good Issue List.
- [ ] A successful operation resets only its own transient-failure counter.
- [ ] Missing `git` and missing `bw` surface immediately with clear, distinct banner copy.
- [ ] A non-Beadwork Workspace surfaces immediately through the refresh banner after it was previously showing a last good snapshot.
- [ ] The empty-workspace state remains banner-free and does not accumulate failures.
- [ ] A stale failure event from a previous Workspace or refresh revision is ignored.

## Test Plan

- Unit-test classification and counter reset semantics for every failure class.
- Test transient failure events followed by recovery: no visible banner before the threshold, banner at the threshold, banner cleared after recovery.
- Test structural-error events: immediate banner with the correct message for missing git, missing bw, and invalid Workspace.
- Frontend tests assert the Issue List remains rendered under the banner and that stale failure events are rejected.
- Add a desktop-level proof that a temporary refresh failure does not replace an already visible Issue List.

# Implementation Plan — bsm-wj1.3

## Goal

Preserve the last successful Issue Explorer snapshot when automatic refresh cannot probe Git or load Beadwork. One through four consecutive transient failures of an operation class remain silent. Strike five shows a non-blocking banner above the Issue List. Missing `git`, missing `bw`, and an invalid Beadwork Workspace bypass the threshold. Refresh failures never replace a rendered `IssueExplorerLoadState` with loading, chooser, or full-pane failure UI.

This slice builds on bsm-wj1.1. It does not implement bsm-wj1.2's per-Workspace SHA cache/switch presentation or bsm-wj1.4's timer/focus triggers.

## Ground truth

- `bw show bsm-wj1.3 --json`
- `docs/adr/0007-refresh-issue-list-by-polling-beadwork-ref.md`
- Backend: `src-tauri/src/refresh.rs`, `src-tauri/src/refresh/tests.rs`, `src-tauri/src/rpc.rs`, `src-tauri/src/workspace.rs`, `src-tauri/src/issues/{adapter,error,runner}.rs`
- Frontend: `src/App.tsx`, `src/workspaces/transition-gate.ts`, `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`, existing App/transition-gate tests and fixtures
- Desktop proof: `e2e/issue-list/scripts/run-scenario.ts`, `e2e/issue-list/fixtures/workspace.ts`, `e2e/issue-list/issue-list.success.spec.ts`, `docs/agents/webdriver-e2e.md`

## Core design

### 1. Publish complete refresh health, not failure/recovery deltas

Keep the existing successful snapshot event and turn it into a two-variant tagged union:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(
    tag = "eventType",
    rename_all = "camelCase",
    rename_all_fields = "camelCase"
)]
enum IssueExplorerRefreshEvent {
    Snapshot {
        issue_data: LoadIssueExplorerDataResponse,
        observed_ref_sha: String,
        refresh_revision: u64,
        workspace_path: String,
        workspace_selection_generation: u32,
    },
    Health {
        health: RefreshHealth,
        refresh_revision: u64,
        workspace_path: String,
        workspace_selection_generation: u32,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct RefreshHealth {
    ref_probe: Option<RefreshFailure>,
    loader: Option<RefreshFailure>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct RefreshFailure {
    error_kind: RefreshFailureKind,
    message: String,
    transient: bool,
    failure_revision: u64,
}
```

`RefreshFailureKind` contains `refProbe`, `loader`, `missingGit`, `missingBw`, and `notBeadworkWorkspace`.

A Health event replaces the renderer's complete two-slot health state. A `null` slot is recovery. There is no Recovery variant, recovery token, embedded snapshot recovery, per-class event watermark, or event-history queue.

Use one process-lifetime monotonic event-revision allocator for logical Snapshot and Health events. Allocate a Snapshot revision when its successful completion is admitted for publication, not when the load starts. A failed transport retry reuses the same logical event/revision. If health changes before an undelivered Health event is retried, discard the obsolete envelope and publish only the latest complete health state with a newer revision.

The renderer keeps separate accepted markers for Snapshot events and Health events. Therefore delivery order between a data snapshot and health state does not affect correctness.

### 2. Keep refresh health in one backend module

Extend `CoordinatorState` with a private health module:

```rust
struct RefreshHealthState {
    binding: RefreshHealthBinding,
    ref_probe_failures: u8,
    loader_failures: u8,
    health: RefreshHealth,
    health_revision: Option<u64>,
    needs_publish: bool,
}
```

`RefreshHealthBinding` distinguishes:

- `Active { path, generation }`
- `SuspendedPending { retained_binding }`
- `IdleNoCurrent`
- `IdleUnavailable`

Pending must retain the previously active binding inside the health module; the Workspace state's generation has already advanced and cannot reconstruct the identity that owned the visible health. Do not derive these states from `Option<(path, generation)>`; the current `current_workspace_binding` returns `None` for both Pending and no Current, which have different behavior.

The health module owns all counter, slot, recovery, rebind, and publication-dirty rules behind a small reducer-style interface. Scheduler callers report operation outcomes; they do not manipulate counters or slots directly.

### 3. Counter and slot rules

- Transient probe failure increments only `ref_probe_failures`.
- Transient loader failure increments only `loader_failures`.
- Counters saturate at five.
- Strikes one through four do not change visible health and do not publish Health events.
- Strike five installs the transient failure in that class's slot, assigns its `failureRevision` from the monotonic allocator, and marks health dirty.
- Later identical failures do not republish the same visible state.
- Missing `git` installs an immediate structural probe failure.
- Missing `bw` and invalid Beadwork Workspace install an immediate structural loader failure.
- A structural failure replaces the visible slot for its class, receives a new `failureRevision`, and starts a new failure episode; reset that class's transient counter to zero.
- Successful probe resets only the probe counter and clears only the probe slot.
- Successful complete All/Ready/Blocked load resets only the loader counter and clears only the loader slot.
- A successful refresh-only Beadwork validity check may clear a structural `missingBw`/`notBeadworkWorkspace` loader slot, but it does not reset or clear a transient loader episode. This lets a repaired dependency recover without waiting for a ref change while preserving the rule that only a complete loader success resets transient loader failures.
- Any visible slot change marks the complete Health state for publication.

When both slots are active, the renderer selects one banner deterministically:

1. structural before transient;
2. within the same category, highest `failureRevision`;
3. stable class tie-breaker only for impossible/equal fixtures.

Clearing the displayed slot reveals the other active slot.

### 4. Binding lifecycle

- **Pending:** suspend probes/loads and preserve counters and visible health.
- **Different Current path:** clear counters and health, bind the new path, and leave SHA/cache behavior to bsm-wj1.2.
- **Same path, new generation:** preserve counters and health, bind the new generation, and mark the complete Health state for republication under the new identity.
- **No Current:** enter idle and clear backend health. The existing Workspace transition clears renderer health when it shows the chooser.
- **Unavailable/deleted Current:** create an empty Health event for the previously rendered identity if the renderer could currently have a banner, then stop probing/loading and clear backend health. If publication fails, retain only that latest empty-state envelope and retry it on later idle ticks until emission succeeds; do not retain event history.

A late old-generation event remains rejectable. If a failed/cancelled switch retains the same Current path under a new generation, the next scheduler turn republishes the complete current health state for that generation, so an old-generation event rejected by the renderer cannot cause permanent drift.

### 5. Preserve typed backend errors

Keep initial/switch loading on the existing `workspace::load_issue_explorer_data -> WorkspaceError` path. Add a refresh-only typed loader that runs All, Ready, and Blocked while retaining the failing view and `ListIssuesError` long enough to normalize it into a cloneable/sendable refresh error.

Classification:

- `ListIssuesError::MissingBinary` -> structural `missingBw`
- `ListIssuesError::NotBeadworkWorkspace` -> structural `notBeadworkWorkspace`
- command exit, parse, and ordinary I/O errors -> transient `loader`
- Git executable missing -> structural `missingGit`
- Git non-zero status, invalid output, and ordinary spawn/I/O failures -> transient `refProbe`

`Command::current_dir(...).output()` can report `NotFound` for either a missing executable or missing working directory. Classification is therefore best-effort:

1. recheck that the bound path is still a readable directory;
2. if unavailable, enter `IdleUnavailable`;
3. if still available, classify the executable as missing;
4. if the path changes during that check, prefer idle/transient behavior over a false structural banner.

### 6. Detect a Workspace that loses Beadwork initialization

A missing/replaced Beadwork ref makes the Git probe fail before the three-view loader can return `NotBeadworkWorkspace`. After an admitted non-zero/invalid-ref probe failure, run one refresh-only `bw config list` validity check for the same binding:

- not initialized/not a Git repository -> immediate structural `notBeadworkWorkspace` in the loader slot;
- missing `bw` -> immediate structural `missingBw` in the loader slot;
- success -> clear an existing structural loader dependency/validity slot, then retain and count the original transient probe failure;
- unrelated validation failure -> leave loader health unchanged and retain/count the original transient probe failure;
- stale/Pending/unavailable binding -> discard or enter idle without changing counters.

While a structural loader slot is active, retry the validity check on later active ticks so repairing `bw` or the Workspace clears the structural banner even when the ref is unchanged. Do not add permanent validity polling when no structural loader slot exists and Git probes are healthy.

"Immediate" means the structural condition bypasses the five-strike budget when a probe, validity check, or loader encounters it. This slice does not continuously probe for a removed `bw` binary while Git is healthy, unchanged, and no loader is needed.

### 7. Keep attempt lifecycle separate from result admission

Replace `LoadBinding.refresh_revision` with an internal attempt ID plus path/generation/SHA binding.

Every completion retires only its matching active attempt, including stale, failed, and unavailable completions. A stale completion must not:

- advance `last_published_sha`;
- consume dirty state belonging to a newer attempt/binding;
- change health counters or slots;
- mutate `runtime.snapshot`;
- publish an event.

Before applying any async probe, validity, or loader result, revalidate path, generation, Pending state, and availability. Before publishing a successful snapshot, repeat the binding/availability check under the runtime mutex. Preserve bsm-wj1.1's single-flight, dirty-follow-up, SHA retry, and backend-snapshot behavior for current admitted successes.

### 8. Use one test seam for external effects

Extend the existing `RefreshOps` seam so tests can inject:

- ref probe;
- Beadwork validity check;
- complete typed refresh loader;
- event publisher.

Production uses `ProcessRunner` and `AppHandle::emit`. Scheduler tests use fakes. This is an internal seam; App, RPC, and renderer callers continue to see only the refresh event contract.

### 9. Renderer admission and startup buffering

Mirror the tagged union in TypeScript and add a small runtime discriminant/shape guard before dispatch. Unknown or malformed events are ignored without mutating snapshot, gate, or health state.

Keep:

- `acceptedRefreshRevision` for Snapshot ordering;
- one `acceptedRefreshHealthRevision` for complete Health-state ordering;
- one `RefreshHealth` renderer state.

Health admission requires a confirmed rendered snapshot, matching path/generation, and a strictly newer health revision. Admission replaces the complete health state and never changes `IssueExplorerLoadState`, Workspace state, or `workspaceKey`.

The listener is registered before startup loading. If a matching Health event arrives before a snapshot identity is confirmed, retain only the newest pre-confirmation Health event in a ref. After startup commits a snapshot, immediately apply the buffered event if path/generation match; otherwise discard it. Clear the buffer on confirmed path change or chooser state.

Pending retains the currently rendered health. A confirmed path change/chooser clears health. A same-path generation rebind preserves the rendered health until the backend republishes the complete state under the new generation.

Use a ref-backed reducer/action helper so the gate marker and health value advance synchronously before React queues presentation state; adjacent transition/health events cannot resurrect cleared health or lose a slot.

### 10. Banner presentation

Add `src/issues/RefreshFailureBanner.tsx` and render it in the Issue Explorer's left pane as a non-scrolling sibling above the search header and list scroll container.

- `data-testid="refresh-failure-banner"`
- `role="alert"`
- no dismiss button
- search remains enabled
- existing Issue rows and sidebar counts remain rendered
- initial full-pane load failure remains unchanged

Canonical backend copy:

- missing Git: `Automatic refresh needs git on PATH to detect Beadwork changes. Install git and restart Beadsmith.`
- missing bw: `Automatic refresh needs bw on PATH to read Beadwork data. Install Beadwork and restart Beadsmith.`
- invalid Workspace: `This Workspace is no longer a Beadwork Workspace. Choose a valid Beadwork Workspace.`
- transient probe: `Automatic refresh is failing while checking Beadwork changes. Retrying…`
- transient loader: `Automatic refresh is failing while reading Beadwork. Retrying…`

## Implementation sequence

```mermaid
graph LR
  A[Typed errors and RefreshOps seam] --> B[Backend health reducer]
  B --> C[Scheduler integration and guarded publication]
  A --> C
  C --> D[Renderer Health admission and startup buffer]
  D --> E[Banner integration]
  E --> F[Desktop failure/recovery proof]
  C --> G[Backend verification]
  D --> H[Frontend verification]
  F --> I[Full verification]
  G --> I
  H --> I
```

### 1. Typed operations and event contract

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/refresh.rs`, `src-tauri/src/refresh/tests.rs`, optionally `src-tauri/src/workspace.rs`

- Add typed probe, validity, and refresh-loader results.
- Add failing-view context for All/Ready/Blocked.
- Extend `RefreshOps` with loader, validity, and publisher adapters.
- Replace the event payload with Snapshot/Health variants and exact camelCase serialization tests.
- Add executable-versus-unavailable-path classification tests.

### 2. Backend health reducer

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/refresh.rs`, `src-tauri/src/refresh/tests.rs`

Test the pure state transitions for:

- strikes one through five and saturation;
- independent probe/loader counters;
- structural replacement and structural recovery;
- operation-class success isolation;
- complete-state dirty publication and latest-state supersession;
- Pending, no Current, unavailable, path replacement, and same-path generation rebind;
- deterministic banner priority inputs.

### 3. Scheduler integration

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/refresh.rs`, `src-tauri/src/rpc.rs`, relevant Rust tests

Using fake `RefreshOps`, prove real scheduler paths for:

- five probe failures -> one visible Health state;
- failed-probe validity fallback;
- immediate structural publication;
- successful probe and successful loader recovery;
- publisher failure followed by latest-state retry;
- startup/current binding guard;
- same-path generation republication;
- stale completion retires its attempt without changing health/SHA/snapshot;
- unavailable completion cannot publish a snapshot;
- existing success, emit-failure, dirty-follow-up, switch, retry, cancel, and stale tests remain green.

### 4. Renderer health state

**Files:** `src/workspaces/transition-gate.ts`, `src/workspaces/transition-gate.test.ts`, add `src/issues/refresh-health.ts` and tests, update fixtures

- Add Health payload validation and admission.
- Add one health revision marker and complete-state replacement.
- Add pre-confirmation buffering and post-startup replay.
- Clear on confirmed path/chooser changes; preserve across Pending and same-path generation rebind.
- Require committed snapshot path and generation to match the Workspace state before rebinding confirmed identity.
- Test stale, malformed, wrong-path, wrong-generation, startup-race, Pending, rebind, and batched-event cases.

### 5. App and banner

**Files:** `src/App.tsx`, `src/issues/RefreshFailureBanner.tsx`, `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`, focused App tests

- Dispatch Snapshot/Health from the existing single listener.
- Keep health updates separate from `issueState` and `workspaceKey`.
- Render the selected failure by structural priority then failure revision.
- Assert `role="alert"`, test ID, non-scrolling sibling placement, enabled search, retained rows/counts/detail/search/view, and automatic clearing.

### 6. Real-desktop proof

**Files:** existing Issue List E2E runner, fixture, helpers, success spec, and E2E docs

- Reuse the existing external mutation in the `issues` scenario; do not add a second mutation that changes the 8/4/2 oracle.
- Add scenario-owned Git/bw PATH wrappers and a control marker.
- Match the failing Git probe argv exactly: `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/beadwork^{commit}`.
- Add a harness-level check proving marker-off pass-through, marker-on exact-probe failure, and pass-through for unrelated Git plus `bw create`/`bw dep add`.
- After a healthy snapshot, enable probe failure, apply the existing external mutation, wait for strike five, and assert the banner plus retained list/current Workspace.
- Remove the marker, wait for the banner to clear and the mutated 8/4/2 snapshot to render.
- Do not use browser refresh, manual load RPCs, or fixed sleeps inside this proof.
- Make provisioning exception-safe and clean all wrappers/control files on success or failure.

## Acceptance traceability

- **1–4 transient failures silent / strike 5 visible:** reducer, scheduler, App, and desktop tests.
- **Only successful class resets:** reducer and App complete-health replacement tests.
- **Missing Git/bw distinct and immediate when encountered:** classifier, scheduler, serialization, and App copy tests.
- **Invalid Workspace immediate after last-good snapshot:** failed-probe validity and typed-loader tests plus App retention test.
- **No Current banner-free:** backend idle and frontend chooser tests.
- **Stale path/generation/revision ignored:** backend revalidation and frontend admission tests.
- **Last good list retained:** App and desktop assertions; health never writes `IssueExplorerLoadState`.
- **Recovery observable:** complete Health state with a cleared slot; no recovery delta/token required.
- **Initial load unchanged:** existing initial loader/full-pane tests plus pre-confirmation health buffering tests.

## Deviation policy

- Do not change Workspace ownership, persistence, initial-load presentation, or bsm-wj1.2 cache semantics to make health fit.
- Retire stale attempts, but never let stale operation results mutate health, SHA, snapshot, or dirty state for another attempt.
- If current Tauri serialization contradicts the tagged-union shape, use separately annotated payload structs and keep serialization tests authoritative.
- Stop if implementation requires a second loader, persisted refresh state, renderer acknowledgements, or an event-history queue; those indicate the full-state design has been bypassed.

## Verification gates

Focused:

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml refresh
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml rpc
pnpm exec vitest run src/workspaces/transition-gate.test.ts src/issues/refresh-health.test.ts src/App.issue-refresh.test.tsx
```

Repository:

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
pnpm test
pnpm check
pnpm exec react-doctor
pnpm test:e2e:issue-list
```

`pnpm test:e2e:issue-list` already builds the desktop binary. At planning time, `pnpm check` has unrelated baseline formatting failures in `.pi/prompts/setup-ralph.md`, `.pi/settings.json`, and five `scratch/` files; this issue must introduce no new failures in touched files.

Before implementation, verify the worktree is clean and bsm-wj1.1 remains the baseline. Final review must specifically check: health never replaces `IssueExplorerLoadState`, counters remain independent, startup health cannot be lost, stale attempts retire safely, unavailable paths cannot publish, complete Health state supersedes obsolete retries, and no recovery-token/event-history machinery was reintroduced.

First commit: backend refresh-health reducer + tagged-union event + frontend admission + banner. 30 reducer tests, 8 banner tests, 8 health admission tests, 3 App integration tests. Backend 170 + frontend 336 tests pass.

Post-review fixup commit: structural loader failures are non-transient (banner priority fix), classifier enums are exhaustive, handle_probe now retries validity check on later active ticks while a structural loader slot is active (plan rule for repair-without-ref-change), and App.tsx hoists the inline RefreshHealth type expression. All 170 backend + 336 frontend tests pass.

title: Preserve the Issue List through automatic refresh failures
